pipelineSettings.saveError: Failed to save settings. Please try again.
pipelineSettings.parallelTasksDescription: How many tasks agents work on simultaneously in this project. Each task runs in its own isolated worktree; more parallelism means more concurrent agent runs (and token/rate-limit usage).
pipelineSettings.sameRepoTitle: Parallel tasks in the same repo
pipelineSettings.sameRepoDescription: When off, tasks touching the same repository run one at a time. Turning it on lets several agents work the same repo in separate worktrees — safe to run, but merge conflicts between their branches become likelier.
pipelineSettings.autoApproveDescription: When on, an approving review from your Code Reviewer agent completes the task and merges automatically. When off, every review waits for your confirmation before merge.
pipelineSettings.autoApprovePlanDescription: When on, the plan your dev agent writes is approved on its own and implementation starts right away — the plan is still written and followed. When off, every plan waits for your approval before work starts.
pipelineSettings.qaDescription: When on, finished development work goes to a Testing lane where your QA agent starts the app and tests the feature in a real browser before code review. Off by default — browser testing uses considerably more tokens.
pipelineSettings.manualVerificationDescription: When on, finished work waits in the Testing lane for you to test it yourself before code review. Approve it or reply with feedback to send it back to development. If QA testing is also on, the QA agent tests first and the task waits for you once it passes.
pipelineSettings.liveDocsDescription: When on, each task that finishes and merges is checked against this project's documents: work worth explaining gets a new document, and a document its changes made wrong gets rewritten. Both are recorded against the task that caused them. Off by default — every completed task costs at least one model call.
pipelineSettings.autoArchiveTitle: Archive done tasks after two weeks
pipelineSettings.autoArchiveDescription: When on, a task that has sat in Done for two weeks is archived automatically, clearing it off the board. Archived tasks are never deleted — you can find them by filtering for archived tasks and restore any of them. Tasks still waiting for their pull request to merge are left alone.
pipelineSettings.runtimeLimitDescription: Off by default: a task runs for as long as the work takes. When on, an agent stopping point is enforced — any run that passes the limit below is stopped and the task is marked failed, keeping a stuck run from burning tokens unattended.
pipelineSettings.runtimeLimitMinutesDescription: How long a single agent run may take before it is stopped. Between {min} and {max} minutes. Each stage of a task (planning, development, review) gets its own run, so this is not the total time a task spends on the board.
pipelineSettings.spendLimitDescription: Off by default. When on, a task whose estimated list-price spend across all of its agent runs reaches the limit below pauses instead of spending more — mid-run (the agent hands off and the work so far stays on the branch) or before its next phase starts, if the estimate is already at the limit. The task then waits for you to choose Continue (one more allotment) or Stop. Nothing half-finished is ever pushed forward as done. Applies to pipeline runs (planning, development, testing, code review); interactive sessions and merge resolution are not capped. Each run is priced at the cost your AI CLI reports or the list price of its tokens; on a subscription nothing is actually charged, so the limit caps usage, not a bill.
pipelineSettings.spendLimitUsdDescription: Estimated list-price spend a task may reach before it asks. Between {min} and {max}. Each Continue grants the same amount again.
pipelineSettings.showToolCallsDescription: When on, the Agent Activity feed on task pages includes every raw tool call the agent makes (file reads, shell commands, searches). Off by default — thinking and progress updates still show without the tool-level noise.
pipelineSettings.qaRunCommandDescription: Command the QA agent runs inside the task's worktree to start the app under test. Without it, QA tasks wait for a human instead.

reposPage.buildDescription: Proves the code still compiles, e.g. "npm run build". Run after Orkka resolves a merge conflict, before the result is pushed — the errors are what let it fix a merge that looks fine but doesn't build. Leave empty to skip the check; it never blocks a merge on its own.

mergePage.title: Two updates changed the same things
mergePage.subtitle: Nothing is broken — pick how to combine them and Orkka takes care of the rest.
mergePage.summaryFallback: This task and a newer update to your app both changed the same {count} file(s).
mergePage.summaryFallbackNoCount: This task and a newer update to your app changed some of the same things.
mergePage.blockedDesc: Orkka can't add this task's changes to your app just yet — your project folder needs a small fix first. Nothing is lost.
mergePage.blockedAutoRetry: Orkka keeps retrying automatically — once it's fixed, this page updates by itself.
mergePage.exhaustedDesc: Orkka tried to combine the two versions several times and checked its own work each time. It couldn't produce a result it was willing to ship, so it stopped instead of guessing.
mergePage.exhaustedNext: You can still pick one side below, or open the task's branch and merge it yourself.
mergePage.combineDesc: AI merges the two versions together, keeping the intent of both. The best choice in almost every case.
mergePage.combineRetryDesc: This is what Orkka just tried and couldn't finish. Worth another go only if you add guidance below telling it what to do differently.
mergePage.guidancePlaceholder: Optional: anything the AI should know (e.g. "keep the new colors")
mergePage.taskDesc: Where the two versions overlap, this task wins. Other recent changes to those parts are replaced.
mergePage.currentTitle: Keep the app as it is
mergePage.currentDesc: Where the two versions overlap, your current app wins. This task's changes to those parts are dropped.
mergePage.advancedHint: Pick which side wins for each file. "AI" lets the assistant merge that file.
mergePage.resolvingDesc: Orkka is merging everything and will finish up automatically. This usually takes a minute or two — you can leave this page.
mergePage.resolvingStrategyTask: Keeping this task's version where they overlap
mergePage.resolvingStrategyCurrent: Keeping your current app where they overlap
mergePage.resolvingStarting: Starting up — the first update appears in a few seconds.
mergePage.resolvingLeaveSafe: Safe to close this page. Orkka keeps going and finishes the merge on its own.
mergePage.steerDesc: Queue a follow-up. It starts the moment this attempt finishes, and only if the merge still hasn't landed — the current one is never interrupted.
mergePage.steerInstead: Or run one of these next instead:
mergePage.resolvedDesc: The changes were combined and merged successfully.

automationPage.title: Automation
automationPage.subtitle: Standing orders for this project — work that happens while nobody is watching.
automationPage.howStep1Body: On its cron or at a set time, on Orkka's clock. Nothing needs to be open on your side.
automationPage.howStep2Body: Exactly like chatting with it: it reads your linked repos and the board, and uses its project tools.
automationPage.howStep3Body: Tasks, documents and diagrams on the project — plus a conversation you can open and reply to.
automationPage.howBoundary: Playbook agents read your code, they never write it. Code only changes when tasks run — that is what an Autopilot window is for.
automationPage.autonomyHint: The master switch for this whole page. Off pauses every schedule and trigger without deleting anything, and “Run now” still works.
automationPage.autonomyPaused: Paused — nothing here is firing on its own.
automationPage.templatesHint: Ready-made schedules bound to this project's agents and skills. Add one, read what it does, then turn it on.
automationPage.templatesFootnote: Each one is added switched off, so nothing runs until you flip its toggle. Edit or delete them like any other schedule.
automationPage.templateAdded: Added — switch it on when you are ready.

groomBacklog.title: Groom the backlog weekly
groomBacklog.body: Your PM reads the Drafting lane and tidies it: duplicates merged, vague titles rewritten, missing acceptance criteria filled in, blocked work flagged.
groomBacklog.message: Groom the Drafting lane: merge duplicates, rewrite vague titles, fill in missing acceptance criteria, and flag anything blocked or oversized.

releaseNotes.title: Friday release notes
releaseNotes.body: Turns the week's finished tasks and merged PRs into user-facing notes, filed as a document on the project.
releaseNotes.message: Write release notes for what shipped this week, grouped as Added / Changed / Fixed, and save them as a document.

securityAudit.title: Weekly security sweep
securityAudit.body: A reviewer reads the codebase for injection, auth gaps, secrets in code and risky dependencies, then files what it finds as tasks.
securityAudit.message: Audit the codebase for security issues: injection, auth and authorization gaps, secrets in code, unsafe deserialization, SSRF and vulnerable dependencies. Report what you find.

dependencyUpdate.title: Dependency check
dependencyUpdate.body: Inventories outdated and vulnerable packages across the project's manifests and proposes a safe order to update them in.
dependencyUpdate.message: Inventory outdated and vulnerable dependencies across the project's package manifests, then propose a safe update plan: patches and minors first, majors flagged separately.

nightShift.title: Autopilot night shift
nightShift.body: Autopilot works the backlog between 22:00 and 06:00 with a $20 cap — the tasks your playbooks filed during the day get built overnight.

automationPage.playbooksHint: An agent takes a scheduled turn, on its own or running one of the project's skills. Its reply lands in a conversation on the Team page.
automationPage.playbooksEmptyHint: For example: Luna grooming the backlog every Monday at 09:00, or an architect drafting release notes every Friday at 17:00.
automationPage.windowsHint: Autopilot works the backlog by itself. Schedule a start and a stop as a pair so it runs for a fixed stretch, under a spend cap.
automationPage.windowsEmptyHint: The usual shape: start at 22:00 with a cap, stop at 06:00 — a night shift on the tasks your playbooks filed.
automationPage.windowsUnpaired: This start has no matching stop. Autopilot keeps going until its cap stops it or nothing is left to pick up.
automationPage.kindPlaybookDesc: An agent takes a turn: reads the repos and board, can file tasks, documents and diagrams.
automationPage.kindAutopilotStartDesc: Opens an Autopilot session so queued tasks start running, under a spend cap.
automationPage.kindAutopilotStopDesc: Closes the session. Work in flight finishes; nothing new is submitted.
automationPage.deleteMessage: "{name}" will stop firing. Past runs stay in the conversation.
automationPage.fieldSkillHint: Runs like typing /slug in chat — the skill's instructions are loaded for this turn.
automationPage.fieldMessagePlaceholder: e.g. Review what shipped this week and draft release notes.
automationPage.fieldMessageHint: What the agent should do this time. With no skill selected, this is the whole instruction.
automationPage.fieldCapHint: Autopilot stops submitting new work once the session has spent this much.
automationPage.uncappedHint: No ceiling on this session — it runs until nothing is left to pick up or you stop it.
automationPage.stopPairHint: Pair this with a start so Autopilot runs for a fixed stretch instead of until the money runs out.
automationPage.fieldWhenHint: Recurring playbooks fire at most every {minutes} minutes.
automationPage.guardrails: Limits: up to {max} schedules per project · a run is skipped when the agent is still busy · {failures} failures in a row disable a schedule.
automationPage.remindersHint: One-shot follow-ups agents set for themselves in chat. They show up here so you can see what is pending — and cancel it.

memoryPage.intro: Agents save durable knowledge here (the remember tool and each run’s outcome); you can add, edit, pin and archive. Pinned entries and Decisions / Conventions / Preferences are shown to every agent on every run; the rest is retrieved by relevance to the task.

welcome.title: Welcome to Orkka
welcome.body: Your project is ready. Here's a quick tour of what each page does — about a minute. You can skip it at any time and it won't come back.

overview.title: Overview
overview.body: The project's home: what your AI team is working on right now, what's waiting on you, and what shipped recently.

team.title: Your AI team
team.body: Every agent on the project — PM, developers, QA, reviewer. Rename them, change their model, tune their instructions, or just chat with one.

activity.title: Activity
activity.body: A live timeline of every agent run: what it did, how long it took, and what it cost.

skills.title: Skills
skills.body: Reusable playbooks your agents can follow. Write one once, assign it to an agent, and it applies to every task they pick up.

automation.title: Automation
automation.body: Schedules, autopilot windows and triggers — let the team pick up work from a GitHub issue or a failing build without you asking.

memory.title: Memory
memory.body: What the project has learned: decisions, conventions, and mistakes worth not repeating. Agents read the relevant ones on every run.

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.body: Milestones and the plan behind them. Group tasks into releases and see where the project is heading.

board.title: Board
board.body: The kanban pipeline. Tasks move from drafting through planning, coding, testing and review — agents move them, you approve the gates.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.body: Every task in one list, with filters and search. This is where you write a new one and hand it to the team.

repos.title: Repos
repos.body: The repositories the project works in. Browse files, read diffs, and set the commands that start each app.

documents.title: Documents
documents.body: Specs, briefs and notes the agents write and read. Upload your own — they become context for every task.

design.title: Design
design.body: Assets Muse creates — logos, icons, illustrations. Approve, reject or ask for another pass; approved assets reach your developers.

architect.title: Diagrams
architect.body: Archie's architecture work: system diagrams, data models and scalability reviews you can edit in place.

settings.title: Project settings
settings.body: Pipeline lanes, autonomy, integrations, and everything else about how this project runs.

inbox.title: Inbox
inbox.body: Everything waiting on a human, across all your projects — questions from agents, plans to approve, reviews to merge.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.body: The full feed, plus where to choose what reaches you by email, Slack or push.

account.title: Settings
account.body: This machine, your trackers, MCP keys and preferences. You can replay this tour from Preferences whenever you like.
